review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its uses in CompactNegativeDeflation.lean and the examples. The simp-tagged lemmas are `differential_apply`, `groupHomologyAddEquivPositive_homologyπ`, `groupHomologyAddEquivFiniteTateNegative_apply` and `groupHomologyAddEquivFiniteTateNegative_isoGroupHomology_apply`. findings.problem: Two @[simp] lemmas have overlapping left-hand sides. The general `_apply` lemma matches every `groupHomologyAddEquivFiniteTateNegative A L S n x`. The specific `_isoGroupHomology_apply` lemma (line 476) matches the same head applied to `(isoGroupHomology ...).app _ .hom x`. Both have default priority and neither is marked as preferred. The general lemma can fire first. That rewrites the term into `(finiteTateNegativeIsoPositiveHomology ..).inv (@groupHomologyAddEquivPositive ... (Fintype.ofFinite _) ... x)`, and the specific lemma then no longer matches. The general lemma also expands a definition into an `eqToIso`-based `.inv` with explicit instance arguments, which is awkward to read in goals. The only use outside this file that I found calls it by name in `simpa only`, so tagging it @[simp] is not needed there.
findings.proposed_change: Remove @[simp] from `groupHomologyAddEquivFiniteTateNegative_apply` and keep it as an explicit unfolding lemma for `rw` or `simp only`, as CompactNegativeDeflation.lean already uses it. Alternatively, give `groupHomologyAddEquivFiniteTateNegative_isoGroupHomology_apply` a higher priority, for example `@[simp high]`, so the Tate-to-compact normal form wins.
findings.benefit: The simp normal form becomes predictable: a Tate class pushed through mathlib's comparison reliably simplifies to `tateCohomologyNegativeAddEquivFiniteTate A L S n x`. Goals are no longer expanded into instance-heavy `eqToIso` expressions.
